title: Impact of Vancomycin-Induced Changes in the Intestinal Microbiota on the Pharmacokinetics of Simvastatin
summary: backgroundthe aim of this study was to investigate the effects of oral vancomycin on the microbiota of healthy subjects.methodssix healthy male subjects were administered oral simcomycin ( 40 mg / kg / day ) for 6 days . <n> fecal samples were collected before and after treatment , and metagenomic analysis was performed to determine the composition of gut microbiota.resultsthe fecal content of s. cerevisiae increased after oral van comycin treatment ( p0.001 ) , while it decreased after simcvastatin treatment . in addition , the relative abundance of fecal metabolites was altered in the study , which included 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo - p - dioxin ( tcdd ) and dimethyl sulfoxide ( dmso).conclusionsthe study suggests that the oral administration of t. comycin results in changes of the gut microbiota in healthy subjects .
key_findings: Oral vancomycin treatment increased the fecal content of S. cerevisiae.
Simvastatin treatment decreased the fecal content of S. cerevisiae.
The relative abundance of fecal metabolites was altered after treatments.
methodology: Six healthy male subjects were administered oral simvastatin (40 mg/kg/day) for 6 days, and fecal samples were collected before and after treatment for metagenomic analysis.
limitations: Study limited to a small sample size of six subjects.
Only male subjects were included, limiting generalizability.
Short duration of treatment may not reflect long-term effects.
future_work: Investigate the effects of vancomycin on a larger and more diverse population.
Explore the long-term impacts of vancomycin on gut microbiota and pharmacokinetics.
Examine the mechanisms behind the changes in fecal metabolites.
